parts.problem_md:
Study Fig. 6.2 of a map showing national parks in Namibia, an LIC in Africa.

![Map of Namibia highlighting national parks and Windhoek. Parks include Bwabwata, Etosha, and Skeleton Coast, with a salt pan in Etosha.](assets/001-map-of-namibia-highlighting-national-parks-and-w.png)

Describe the location of the following three national parks in Namibia.

1. Dorob
2. Bwabwata
3. Etosha
parts.solution_md:
1. Dorob is along the coast, 200–300 km west of Windhoek. **[1]**
2. Bwabwata is in the northeast, 600–800 km from Windhoek, between the borders of Angola and Botswana. **[1]**
3. Etosha is in the central north, surrounding a salt pan between 400 and 450 km NNW of Windhoek. **[1]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> **Mark allocation**
> 
> - **1 mark [1]** per developed point.

parts.problem_md:
Study Fig. 6.1, a map of the Meru National Park in Kenya, an LIC in east Africa.

![Map of Meru National Park showing tourist roads, rivers, campsites, gates, and key locations like the Rhino Sanctuary and park headquarters.](assets/002-map-of-meru-national-park-showing-tourist-roads-.png)

Estimate the area of Meru National Park in square kilometres.
parts.solution_md:
**B**** **is the correct answer.

The alternative answers are incorrect because:

- **A: **This is slightly smaller than the city of Chicago.
- **C: **This is roughly twice the size of London.
- **D: **This is the size of Jamaica.

> **[exam-tip]**
> When working out size, quickly try to visualise what it would look like to give you a sense of scale. Take answer D for instance. Imagine a square where each side measures 100 kilometres; this represents a large area. Alternatively, think of a very large number of smaller areas you know, like 10,000 football fields. Far larger than the park could be.
> 
> This is just a quick way of comparing data to size and helps save time in the exam.

parts.problem_md:
Study the map extract showing part of Kingston, Jamaica (scale 1:50 000). Jamaica is an LIC.

[Map extract](https://www.cambridgeinternational.org/Images/719016-2027-specimen-paper-survey-map-2.pdf)

Using map evidence, suggest **two **advantages and **two **disadvantages of the location of Norman Manley International Airport.
parts.solution_md:
Two advantages are:

1. The airport is on flat land, which is necessary for the runway and buildings. **[1]**
2. It is easy to get to because there is a main road access. **[1]**

Two disadvantages are:

1. There is a limited amount of land to build on. **[1]**
2. It is liable to damage from storms and flooding. **[1]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> The command word is ‘**suggest**’; this means you need to consider both the advantages of building the airport in its current location and the potential disadvantages.
> 
> **Mark allocation**
> 
> - 1 mark **[1]** per valid point.
> 
> **Alternative content**
> 
> Other ideas that could be used are:
> 
> - Planes approach over sea, which protects buildings and people in the event of an accident.
> - Planes do not have to approach over the built-up area, which lessens pollution.
> - It is a long journey from Kingston along a sandspit.
> - The exposed coastal area could be susceptible to high tides and tropical storm damage.
